title: Core: Fix onboarding visual bugs, survey telemetry and modal dismissal
body:

<!--

Thank you for contributing to Storybook! Please submit all PRs to the `next` branch unless they are specific to the current release. Storybook maintainers cherry-pick bug and documentation fixes into the `main` branch as part of the release process, so you shouldn't need to worry about this. For additional guidance: https://storybook.js.org/docs/contribute

## What I did

- Fixed some visual bugs related to the guided tour tooltips attempting to highlight elements outside the viewport, by ensuring the panel height is set correctly.
- Fixed controls panel scrolling + sticky bar behavior.
- Improved controls panel styling for better visual consistency.
- Added "openSurvey" telemetry event for more reliable completion rate tracking.
- Fixed Modal close button triggering form submission due to missing `type` attribute.
- Fixed survey dismissal behavior to ensure modal stays closed.

comments.author: ndelangen
comments.body:
I have a bit of an (non blocking) issue with this code.
I understand you're trying to change the styling of something rendered internally to this component.

Can you explain why an override is the right approach?
Is this styling change/override only desirable here, in the ControlPanel component?
The ArgsTable-component is also a doc-block, why would this styling change not be applied there?

Personally I see styling overrides a bit like a code-smell, because it results in more inconsistencies over time.
I'd prefer components to be self-reliant, influenced only by explicits API's (such as props, context, and explicit classNames) (with a very strong preference for props).

Here's the element you're targetting AFAICS:
https://github.com/storybookjs/storybook/blob/9ff887c4e4b3de8cf42ec8bfb3fca511f0eb7d2d/code/addons/docs/src/blocks/components/ArgsTable/ArgsTable.tsx#L405
comments.label_reasoning: The comment critiques the use of CSS styling overrides to modify internal component styles, arguing for self-reliant components with explicit APIs (props, context, classNames). This is fundamentally a class/component design concern about encapsulation and proper API boundaries.

comments.author: ghengeveld
comments.body: For the backgroundColor I can't avoid the override, because it's specific to the ControlsPanel instance of ArgsTable, and ArgsTable doesn't accept className so I can't use a custom styled component. I've at least moved the lineHeight to ArgsTable because I do think that should just apply to all of them.

review_threads.actionability_reasoning: The comment raises a concern about styling overrides being a code smell and suggests that the component should be influenced only by explicit APIs (props, context, classNames). This implies a concrete change: refactor the styling override to use a proper prop-based API instead of directly targeting internal elements.
